LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.exists_expurgated: Suppose a sequence of block codes for W has Mₙ ≥ 1 messages at length n, and W has a finite output alphabet. Let eₙ be the error probability averaged uniformly over the Mₙ messages. Assume eₙ tends to zero and the rate is eventually at least R − δ for every δ > 0. Retain exactly the messages with individual error at most 2eₙ and index them by an injection into the original message set. Redirect discarded decoder outputs to the retained message with new index zero. The resulting code has at least ⌈Mₙ/2⌉ messages and maximal error at most 2eₙ, so its maximal error tends to zero. At positive lengths its rate loss is at most (ln 2)/n, preserving the eventual rate bounds.
